source_contract_finding.best_public_source_contract: DataSF dual-feed remains the correct public contract. Use historical dataset tmnf-yvry for incident date < 2018-01-01 and current dataset wg3w-h783 for incident date >= 2018-01-01. In the current dataset keep only Initial, Coplogic Initial, and Vehicle Initial rows; dedupe on incident_number + v2_offense; exclude Out of SF rows; apply the homicide and recovered-vehicle exclusions; and add three small 2025 packet-local overrides.

evidence.finding: Historical dataset metadata still says the legacy CABLE feed was discontinued in May 2018 and directs 2018+ users to the new Crime Data Warehouse-backed dataset.

Current dataset metadata still says incident locations are mapped to nearby intersections for anonymity and warns that rows before versus after 2024-04-24 use slightly different snapped intersections.
The historical feed still contains 43,733 rows dated 2018, so the 2018-01-01 hard cutover remains necessary.
The 2025 late feed still mixes 81,496 initial-like rows with 13,341 supplement rows, so explicit report-type filtering remains mandatory.

manual_2025_additions.incident_description: Burglary, Hotel Room, Att. Forcible Entry

notes: The legacy category+description join still carries the San Francisco packet. No broader remap was needed.
The only offense-relevant late-feed additions discovered in the live 2025 feed were the three small burglary/larceny descriptions listed above.
Packet-local manual exclusions still apply for homicide manslaughter and excusable homicide rows, plus recovered vehicles stolen outside San Francisco.

spatial_contract_finding.block_group_strategy: Use the published latitude/longitude and join to Census block groups. Do not geocode from address as a first resort because DataSF already publishes snapped coordinates.
spatial_contract_finding.fallback: Rows with police_district = Out of SF or missing snapped coordinates should not be block-group allocated. Larceny is the only promotable offense with material missing-coordinate loss; the other promotable offenses are essentially fully allocable.
spatial_contract_finding.privacy_note: Current-feed incident locations are privacy-snapped to nearby intersections, and DataSF still flags a snapping-method change on 2024-04-24.

reconciliation_finding.reference_window: Use the official citywide YTD 2024 and YTD 2025 tables in the December 2025 CompStat PDF. This is the latest official public comparator currently available and it revises the 2024 year-end totals upward from the January 2025 PDF.
reconciliation_finding.high_level_result: Five-offense selective promotion is supportable now. Robbery, aggravated_assault, burglary, larceny, and motor_vehicle_theft all stay within about +/-10 percent of the official citywide counts after hardening across both revised 2024 and 2025. Murder and rape remain severe undercounts.
reconciliation_finding.exact_offense_boundary: Promote robbery, aggravated_assault, burglary, larceny, and motor_vehicle_theft on hardened allocable rows only. Keep murder and rape blocked.

production_assessment.reason: Full-city promotion remains blocked because murder and rape are irreducibly undercounted in the public feed, but a production-usable offense-selective boundary now exists for five offenses.
builder_support_required: Add an offense-selective San Francisco gate instead of relying on full-city packet promotion only.

Implement the San Francisco dual-feed builder path with the 2018-01-01 cutover, initial-only report-type filter, incident_number+v2_offense dedupe, Out of SF exclusion, documented homicide and recovered-vehicle exclusions, and the three 2025 packet-local overrides.
Do not force missing-coordinate rows into block groups. Drop them or retain them as city-level residuals outside the allocable surface. This requirement matters most for larceny.

generalizable_doctrine_findings.finding: When an agency publishes a later year-end CompStat PDF that revises the prior year, the revised prior-year table is usually the better comparator than the earlier year-end PDF.

sf_evidence.effect: The revised 2024 larceny and motor-vehicle-theft totals move substantially closer to the hardened live-feed counts and change the offense-selective boundary.

generalizable_doctrine_findings.finding: A city can remain blocked for full-city use while still supporting a broad property-plus-robbery selective path if the hardened allocable rows reconcile across multiple official years.

Raw public homicide rows can look superficially close to an official homicide total, but initial-only hardening can reveal that the public feed is not publishing a usable one-row-per-victim homicide line.
